keySentence: Shared laws and values create genuine belonging.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: The human village had pushed Mowgli away because he seemed strange. He walked back to the jungle with a heavy and sad heart. Baloo and Bagheera met him at the edge of the trees. They did not ask where he had been or what had happened. They asked only if he still remembered the Law of the Jungle. When Mowgli recited it perfectly they led him home at once. Shared laws and values create genuine belonging.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: When Mowgli was rejected by the human village he returned to the jungle with a heavy heart. The villagers had feared him because he was different and had grown up among animals. But the jungle welcomed him back because he still knew and still honored its ancient Law. Baloo and Bagheera met him at the tree line and did not ask him where he had been. They asked only if he still remembered the words and the duties that the Law required. When Mowgli recited them perfectly both animals nodded and led him home without another word. It was not blood or appearance that made him one of them — it was the values they all shared. Shared laws and values create genuine belonging.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: The day Mowgli was rejected by the human village was one of the hardest days of his young life. The villagers had looked at him with suspicion from the start — his strange manners, his knowledge of the animals, the way he moved through the forest without fear. He returned to the jungle with a heavy heart, expecting that perhaps he no longer belonged there either after so much time away. But Baloo and Bagheera were waiting for him at the edge of the trees, and they did not ask him where he had been or why. They asked him only a single question — whether he still remembered the words of the Law of the Jungle that they had taught him as a cub. Mowgli recited every article of it without hesitation, and when he had finished both animals nodded and led him back into the shadows of the forest. It was not his appearance that made him one of them, nor his blood, nor his history, nor his physical resemblance to any jungle creature. It was the fact that he still carried within him the same values and the same commitments that defined every genuine member of the jungle. Shared laws and values create genuine belonging.
